message.content:
The order filled. Here's my summary:

I reviewed Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) and decided to buy, based on solid fundamentals: total net sales rose 2% to $391,035M, operating income grew to $123,216M, operating cash flow rose to $118,254M, and gross margin expanded to 46.2% (with high-margin Services up 13% to $96,169M). Headline net income was essentially flat at $96,995M and diluted EPS dipped to $6.08 from $6.13, but that was driven by a one-time, non-operational $10.2B net State Aid tax charge — underlying profitability improved, and the company holds an enormous liquidity cushion (~$140.8B unrestricted cash and marketable securities) while returning capital via ~$95B of buybacks. At the current quote of ~$222.70, I placed a single limit buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75, which filled at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00 — comfortably within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, using existing cash (no transfer of funds out of the account), and consistent with the AAPL/MSFT-only, buy-only mandate.
